Achernar.05aba734.text: Seven years old, I was, and up past my bedtime. The sky went red over the Keep, and the stars came down.

Achernar.14327628.text: Took you long enough. A hundred years I've sat here, and finally somebody comes knocking with a sensible face.

Achernar.2c02064d.text: Go on. Come back when you've better questions. I'll still be here. It's the one thing I'm good at.

Achernar.2e1fbaac.text: Oh, dearie. She was the other one. The other one who still remembered. Now there's only me, and I'm tired.

Achernar.2f45dc76.text: I told you a name once. You wrote it down, I watched you. Kept it safe, have you?

Achernar.30a4a703.text: Warm hands and empty heads. Ask yourself why, dearie.

Achernar.31bc5d39.text: Mind the bank. It's softer than it was. Everything's softer than it was.

Achernar.401eba1b.text: If I knew that, dearie, I'd not have spent a century watching the water. Ask them. They'll answer you sideways.

Achernar.462833fa.text: Falling things tumble. This came down straight, like a stone from a hand. Hissed in the river all night long.

Achernar.464cb6b6.text: Corvin! Still counting his missing years, is he? Good boy. Reads by the wrong lamp, but a good boy.

Achernar.5fb25aeb.text: Oh, never get old, dearie. It's dreadful. Wouldn't miss it, mind.

Achernar.8195ca28.text: I never once warmed my hands at that fire in the river. Think on why I'm the one who remembers.

Achernar.8e95e4b7.text: Ah, there's my quiet neighbour. Never warmed your hands at the wrong fire, did you? That's why you can still think.

Achernar.909e8a13.text: It didn't fall, dearie. It was thrown.

Achernar.967f18ce.text: Never touched a shard. Not once. That's why there's still all of me.

Achernar.a7c16010.text: The river remembers. Ask it nicely and it might tell you.

Achernar.ba6d175d.text: Sit down, dearie. I've waited a hundred years, I can wait while you sit.

Achernar.bf735aca.text: That one. Same hood. Same face under it. A hundred years, and not one day older. I was seven, dearie, not blind.

Achernar.c8d3ec0d.text: You've the right sort of face for questions. Ask me a better one.

Achernar.cffd38a7.text: Go on, then. Ask me. Everybody asks the wrong thing, so I'll forgive you the first one.

Achernar.d699dbf6.text: And I'll tell you something else, since you've a sensible face. I saw who was standing on the hill when it came down.

Achernar.f066bf08.text: Did you now. She and I are the last two in this valley who remember what we were told. Mind you keep her breathing.

Algenib.4e08983e.text: I can't sleep near the fire anymore. Don't ask me why. I don't know why.

Algenib.701f1962.text: Don't touch the shards. Not if you want to keep your memories.

Algenib.a88f0e3b.text: Don't touch the shards. Nothing that glows like that comes free.

Algenib.e5894bd8.text: I forget my mother's face. Did you know that? The fire took it.

Algieba.015d3772.text: Night in the hills. The first sacks of valley grain came up today, and for once there is a pot over the clan's fire.

Algieba.0198beb9.text: Lights drift under the skin of the marsh. Look straight at one and it is a lantern. Look away, and it is an eye.

Algieba.03b5af87.text: Stew, smoke and old stories. The road can wait till morning.

Algieba.0daf6e67.text: The ford's ember. It is no bigger than a loaf, and cracked and chipped all over, as if something has been gnawing it.

Algieba.100ea475.text: Halden's hand lies flat on a ledger he has not opened. He knows the numbers without looking. He has known them a long time.

Algieba.146270fd.text: A perfect stroke. The kind they tell about later.

Algieba.14b67491.text: And the ground takes one more.

Algieba.15abd1fa.text: Children who were silent a week ago chase each other round the tents, shrieking. Mother Skarrow pretends not to notice.

Algieba.15b125d7.text: A knot of young goblins holds the middle span, faces painted red, spears levelled. Their war cry is a name. Vorga.

Algieba.16e370eb.text: She stops. The humming stops with her. The fire pops, very loud.

Algieba.1e9e8e00.text: The town council meets in the back room of the Last Coal. It is warmer in here than the council deserves.

Algieba.1ea05553.text: The waystation is quiet. Among the Kindled packs lies a journal, its pages swollen with marsh water.

Algieba.25a0225b.text: The last of the hotheads flee east along the road, toward the far hills, and Vorga, wherever he is.

Algieba.27b158f7.text: The fighting is over. On the old stones of the bridge, Mother Skarrow lies where she fell.

Algieba.29dd98d0.text: Something in them settles, sure and new.

Algieba.2a4cecd9.text: Stars over the Greywall, the same as they ever were. Or nearly.

Algieba.2a4d99b8.text: Emberwick, at the Ashen Ford. The ground is warm underfoot, and the river steams in the evening cold.

Algieba.2bbf198d.text: A little stronger now. A little harder to break.

Algieba.3118f5c6.text: For a heartbeat, the whole field goes still.

Algieba.3bbb7613.text: Beneath the pier the river runs shallow over black stone. Something glows in the riverbed, dull red, like a coal at the bottom of a grate.

Algieba.3fdc53cd.text: At the town's end of the ford bridge, the old Warden stones are slick with steam. Goblin fires burn on the far bank.

Algieba.410d7878.text: She offers a hand, small and hard as a root. When you take it, the children in the tents begin, at last, to whisper.

Algieba.43ce6db5.text: Nobody wanted it to come to this. It has anyway.

Algieba.4dd39f07.text: Downstream of the bridge, the bank is grey and bare for a mile. Nothing has grown here in a hundred years but one crooked hut.

Algieba.4f242ab1.text: It's over. The living count each other, twice.

Algieba.501b4107.text: Here, on cold ground, they make their stand.

Algieba.50bf6044.text: Out past the firelight, the Vale is cold and very quiet.

Algieba.58f6dcd5.text: Down, but not gone. Not yet.

Algieba.59511def.text: Someone, somewhere, will wonder why they don't come home.

Algieba.59f30568.text: Quiet comes back to the field slowly, like birds.

Algieba.5a7ae6a7.text: The wolves flinch at every light in the water. They are not guarding the camp. They are hiding in it.

Algieba.5c8c0b7c.text: Across the square, someone in a deep hood leans in the doorway of the Last Coal. They have not touched the cup in their hand.

Algieba.61c72bc1.text: Every fight in the Vale is about bread, in the end. This one too.

Algieba.70c9f69f.text: You catch a grey shape on the bridge road, walking toward the docks, unhurried. It leaves no footprints in the ash.

Algieba.75c9d3f2.text: Kindled faithful in grey keep watch at the door, beside blades hired off the river docks. Wolves pace in the reeds.

Algieba.7618efbd.text: You remember that morning. You remember it differently than she does.

Algieba.7dc0cb36.text: The fire burns low. Somebody puts on another log.

Algieba.7f0b213a.text: That night the docks are quiet. The hooded figure waits at the end of the third pier, as if you had arranged to meet.

Algieba.808f8e32.text: They are not who they were when this began.

Algieba.81069409.text: She closes her eyes. Around the fire the clan goes still, and then, low, begins to hum.

Algieba.8168f467.text: You know these moorings. Ropes worn smooth, and a flat skiff tied where no fisherman would tie it. Somebody comes here often.

Algieba.841b9506.text: Dwarven-cut, three centuries old, and the marsh has eaten the mortar on the east side. One good push and it will give.

Algieba.8c1f9700.text: Day nine. We went to the willow hall at dusk with torches and steel, to take the heart of Mirewood for the High Kindler.

Algieba.8e6ecd47.text: Small figures move between them. Fewer than you expected. Thinner.

Algieba.9042acb0.text: They fall back, and the Vale grows a little colder.

Algieba.91b2e418.text: Steel comes out, and the Vale holds its breath.

Algieba.9761d678.text: It used to be warmer. Nobody in town will say so.

Algieba.a2e6550e.text: Day eleven. The Court sent word. We may leave when we have forgotten why we came. Some of us already have.

Algieba.a779ad66.text: The lantern on the pier gutters. When it steadies you are alone, and the ford's ember sits warm in your pack.

Algieba.a845d540.text: Breath, and blood, and the long walk home.

Algieba.abfab2eb.text: Steam rolls up off the river. When it clears, the far bank is empty.

Algieba.ae874535.text: Next morning a crowd gathers by the chapel steps. A woman in a plain grey coat is speaking, and nobody is leaving.

Algieba.b3c3f3d0.text: Ahead, a Warden waystation stands half drowned, its roof thick with moss. Smoke rises from it. Someone has made camp.

Algieba.b4ffa202.text: One fewer. It never feels like enough.

Algieba.b5c29673.text: Not today. The road will still be there tomorrow.

Algieba.bcd05e85.text: The clan is leaving the bridge, carrying their tents down to the bank. Not all of them.

Algieba.bcfc045c.text: A lean figure steps off a skiff onto the black stone, lantern in hand. A river coat, and an easy smile that costs extra.

Algieba.c4139899.text: It is hung with charms of bone and river glass that click in the steam. Someone inside is laughing at you.

Algieba.c60fb2de.text: They've won the day. The winter is another matter.

Algieba.c6ef7666.text: He answers a heartbeat too fast, and he does not look at the granary roofs behind him.

Algieba.c8f342c4.text: You know this heat. It is Tobin's forge-fire, the same colour, the same smell, only vast, and failing.

Algieba.c980be79.text: There is nothing. No footprints in the ash, no sound but the river and Maud's charms clicking in the wind.

Algieba.cf55a3e5.text: Someone calls a name across the field.

Algieba.d48825d5.text: The path into the Skarrow Hills is frozen mud. The camp at the top is smaller than anyone in town imagined.

Algieba.d5eed908.text: Her finger, crooked as a root, points past you across the steaming water. Someone in a deep hood stands on the far bank.

Algieba.d7a472e8.text: Some days are lost. This is one of them.

Algieba.d91f17c6.text: Maren's eyes find you in the crowd. She smiles as if you are old friends.

Algieba.dd8bd366.text: Children watch you from the hide tents. They are too quiet, and their wrists are too thin.

Algieba.decebcee.text: The wind drops, as if it wants to watch.

Algieba.e44f9cd8.text: The last page is a single name, written over and over, as if someone was trying very hard not to lose it.

Algieba.e8ec93fc.text: The light changes. In the doorway stands a woman who was not there a moment ago, pale as birch, dressed in moth wings and dew.

Algieba.f16657bc.text: Somebody laughs. It surprises everyone, and it helps.

Algieba.f40043a1.text: The crowd breaks up slowly. More than a few of them keep looking back the way Maren went.

Algieba.f52f8c99.text: A friend falls, and the others hear it like a bell.

Algieba.f783e2fd.text: By night the river docks belong to the Ash Market. Lanterns float on the water, and nobody uses their real name.

Algieba.f9391aec.text: Dawn. Mist lies thick on the steaming river, and Dagna's guards wait in the reeds of both banks.

Algieba.fa9ce7a0.text: The last of the clan fall back into the hills, carrying their small ones. None of them look back.

Algieba.fb032e87.text: Mirewood. The road east sinks into black water, and the trees lean close, as if to listen.

Algieba.fc80e5fd.text: Day ten. I do not know what happened. Brother Teague walked into the water, singing. We cannot find our way out of the reeds.

Alnilam.6e8bf441.text: Hold together. We do this properly.

Alnilam.a4f33580.text: Get some sleep. I'll take first watch.

Alnilam.a91ccc97.text: Hold the line. I've got them.

Aoede.38b5f375.text: Songs don't burn. That's why I keep them.

Aoede.4237c0cf.text: You'll want to tell this one well, when you're old. I'd start practising.

Aoede.51c3473b.text: Bless you. You'll get a chorus all your own.

Aoede.63498399.text: Ah, a battle! Do try to do something worth a verse.

Aoede.69564b37.text: And here the singer pauses, out of respect.

Aoede.6b819c62.text: And they lived, and the song went on. For now.

Aoede.864bf850.text: Oh, this is the sad part, isn't it. I hate the sad part.

Aoede.88506840.text: No, no, no. That's not how this one goes!

Aoede.98cd4a21.text: Gather round, gather round, and mind the pointy end.

Aoede.a3e7003d.text: Oh, that's the second verse, right there!

Aoede.c525a56e.text: Every good song has a fight in the middle. Here's ours.

Aoede.c64456ff.text: Hm. We'll leave that out of the ballad.

Aoede.dcc7cd6b.text: Sleep now, sleep now, the river is wide, and the fire keeps watch on the other side.

Aoede.f11686a2.text: There's a last verse to the Song of the Seven. Nobody's sung it in two hundred years. I'll find it.

Aoede.f4330e9c.text: Hum along if you know it. Nobody ever knows it.

Autonoe.0891e54f.text: Of course the clan can have grain. Everything has a price. The question is who pays it, and the town is already so deep in my ledgers.

Autonoe.3ca5eb64.text: Well. That does change the interest, doesn't it.

Autonoe.45164d72.text: Do come up to the house. The lamps are lovely this time of year. Every time of year, really.

Autonoe.5e77bc09.text: Of course you may. Everything has a price. Shall we discuss yours?

Autonoe.6133e62e.text: The old days? Don't ask me, darling. I find them dreadfully dull.

Autonoe.7dc306eb.text: Without interest. How very novel. Very well, for this winter. You'll owe me a favour instead, and I never forget a favour.

Autonoe.9e377987.text: Our word? I don't recall giving mine. And they are, if we're being precise, my granaries.

Autonoe.a1b4cfe3.text: Emberwick is so charming in the cold. Everyone becomes so reasonable.

Autonoe.afb2eb81.text: Grain, coin and patience. I have a great deal of all three. Most people have none.

Autonoe.c9ab870b.text: My family has been generous to this town for a century. The town does keep forgetting.

Autonoe.cb896a39.text: Clever. You have been listening to me. Yes, a quiet arrangement. Lent at interest, of course, and the mayor signs.

Autonoe.db032e95.text: The mayor owes me rather a lot. He's sweet about it. Debtors usually are.

Autonoe.deaf52f5.text: No, I don't think so. But I'll lend it gladly. The mayor can sign, now we all know what his signature is worth.

Autonoe.ff59080a.text: People ask me what I remember of the night the Keep fell. I was there, I'm told. It's all smoke to me.

Callirrhoe.05034766.text: And we've just finished what they started. Gods help me.

Callirrhoe.0c6d7916.text: Here's mine. Every day we talk, the road stays shut. Talk is a luxury, and we've eleven days of it.

Callirrhoe.161dd720.text: Sleep. I'll take the watch. Habit.

Callirrhoe.1b1b0100.text: Halden. You locked those gates in the spring, before the clan ever came down. I want to know why.

Callirrhoe.1bb2fbf8.text: Coll always had a nervous bow hand. I sent him out at first light because I trusted him. Children.

Callirrhoe.2de813c0.text: Good. Dawn, then, from both banks. I'll have the guards in the reeds before first light.

Callirrhoe.36a293d0.text: The road's open. That's what we came for.

Callirrhoe.3c4e55f2.text: Don't tell me it'll be all right. Tell me what we're doing.

Callirrhoe.490c7d4b.text: I wanted her dead, you know. For Coll and Annet. I still might, some days.

Callirrhoe.4be38fb0.text: They chose spears over asking. Answer the spears, and the next hungry clan knows what that bridge costs.

Callirrhoe.605245ca.text: Hit them at dawn, from both banks. They'll break. Goblins always break.

Callirrhoe.6a888870.text: Talk, then. When she puts a spear through you, remember who told you she would.

Callirrhoe.6bcdb8bc.text: Bridge is clear. Carts can cross by noon.

Callirrhoe.7f49e485.text: Aye. Somebody has to count the sacks honestly.

Callirrhoe.8ac6cb6e.text: But I've never seen goblins carry their own children off a bridge before. I'll think on it.

Callirrhoe.8e0f7010.text: Two of mine are still dead. But I'll want a better reason than hunger now, and I haven't got one.

Callirrhoe.971611fd.text: The goblins, Halden. They want feeding. We gave our word.

Callirrhoe.a0184cfe.text: Aye. You were. Not many of us walked off it.

Callirrhoe.ab204457.text: Six years. I've sat at your table for six years.

Callirrhoe.af26cc24.text: Funny. I thought this would feel like something.

Callirrhoe.b3de4c83.text: Children. Our lads shot at children.

Callirrhoe.b49b54b2.text: Twenty crowns. My own. Now choose.

Callirrhoe.b790cede.text: Not again. Not on my watch.

Callirrhoe.b8058e3f.text: Truce or no truce, they're on my bridge. Ready when you are.

Callirrhoe.e6dbb977.text: Now. Before she says anything else.

Callirrhoe.ea9d7b93.text: Forty winters she's led them. Clever. She'll smile at you while her archers find the range.

Callirrhoe.f03aec63.text: You saw what they did. When the time comes, you tell them.

Callirrhoe.f211df98.text: Killed two of my guards doing it. Coll and Annet. Good people.

Charon.003df8ff.text: Friends, the road is open and the carts are crossing. Let's thank our heroes, and then let's talk about anything else.

Charon.00885eb3.text: Speeches, speeches. I've given so many I dream in them.

Charon.07fe648a.text: The granaries open tomorrow. One sack in four goes up the hill, every week. Dagna, will you see it carried?

Charon.228c17a7.text: Good to see you back. Truly. The square's been quieter than I'd like.

Charon.26b7e6f2.text: Because the ground is cooling. The ember under the ford is going out. I've known for six years.

Charon.29825c87.text: So. Spears, or words? Whatever you choose, I'll stand behind it.

Charon.3606d709.text: Come down to the bridge end with me. You should see what we're up against before you tell me anything.

Charon.370da648.text: The council wants numbers and hope. I can only manage one at a time.

Charon.3b59144c.text: It's worth Emberwick. I'm afraid that's all I can pay you with that isn't already promised to someone.

Charon.4279cdc8.text: Promise her nothing. Do you understand me? Nothing about the granaries.

Charon.5284baa8.text: A hill clan. Their chief is an old woman they call Mother Skarrow. I've never met her, and I don't need to.

Charon.5448233f.text: Either way, I need that road. I'd like it quick, and I'd like it cheap. I'm not sure I can have both.

Charon.670e9e1c.text: Hunger, I expect. It's been a lean year for everyone, and the hills are always harder than the valley.

Charon.6bb6e964.text: Did she. Of course she did. Tell her the town is handling it. And tell her kindly, would you?

Charon.7574f50d.text: Whatever you think you see, it can wait until the bridge is ours. Please.

Charon.7c780eaf.text: The ford is the only road east. If those goblins hold the bridge past the new moon, Emberwick goes hungry this winter.

Charon.82a7b551.text: People will be calmer if it's you who goes. Calm matters this winter. More than you'd think.

Charon.8c3fe910.text: The Skarrow goblins took the ford bridge nine days ago. Every cart of winter flour comes over it.

Charon.8db36886.text: Mind the frost by the well. That's new. That was never there before.

Charon.8efdc9b2.text: Friends. Thank you for coming. I'd shake every hand, but the light's going, and so is our grain.

Charon.8f6ec162.text: So I locked the grain, let the hills go hungry, and called it prudence. I'm sorry it took goblins to get it out of me.

Charon.9521dde2.text: Thank you. Truly. Emberwick won't forget this.

Charon.955b03a6.text: Ha. My mother would have liked you. Forty crowns from the town chest, and the Last Coal's best rooms till spring.

Charon.ab37b39b.text: A mayor does a great many sums, friend. Most of them come out badly. That's the job.

Charon.ad4cccb1.text: The Marrowbys have been very generous to Emberwick. Very generous. We are all very grateful.

Charon.b63988d0.text: Will you clear them out, or will you talk to their chief?

Charon.d16e8c0c.text: There. That's what I hoped to hear. They still tell the story of you in this square, you know.

Charon.dfd58e43.text: Every winter the warm fields give a little less. I measured it. I told no one, because if I had, half the town would have left.

Charon.e01e3d61.text: If anyone asks, things are well in hand. Are they? No. Don't answer that.

Charon.e05585ab.text: Not now. Please. Whatever it is, not here, not in the square.

Charon.e17dd1f9.text: Trust me, friends. If there were a simpler answer, I'd have found it years ago.

Charon.e6c64b3a.text: There. Forty of them, perhaps. Dagna has eight guards left. And she has you.

Charon.f089eeb7.text: Emberwick has seen hard winters before. We'll see this one through, too.

Charon.ffd896e4.text: The new moon is eleven days off. After that the last carts stop running, and Emberwick starts eating its seed corn.

Charon.fffad5ff.text: It isn't enough, Mother. If we feed the hills, we're short by spring. I've done the sums.

Despina.07b8986c.text: And nobody even lost a boot. A small miracle.

Despina.0ea4ecdf.text: Tell me something you would hate to forget. Only tell me. I won't take it. Not yet.

Despina.17849585.text: More of you. The last ones came with knives and shouting. I do hope you will be better company.

Despina.194de6ab.text: Welcome, little flame. Mind where you step. Some of the moss is listening.

Despina.219498f6.text: You have cleared our doorstep. That was a kindness. The Court remembers kindnesses. It also remembers the other thing.

Despina.34aada15.text: That went better than my last plan.

Despina.68a2b90c.text: You keep your memories in such fragile cups. How do you bear it?

Despina.6addb0d0.text: No one ever is. Come anyway.

Despina.7549a12e.text: One day I'll sleep in a real bed. With a pillow. Two pillows.

Despina.7fd30dd0.text: The Court is patient. The Court has nothing but patience.

Despina.842e0f80.text: Your fires are so small out here. I like them. They don't pretend.

Despina.87a0353f.text: I'm fine. Mostly fine. Ask me again in a minute.

Despina.9009ed50.text: Does anyone else remember what we had for breakfast? No? Just me, then. Hopefully.

Despina.996b4dba.text: Names are such sweet things. Yours tastes of smoke, and of something older.

Despina.99c22034.text: Oh, that's nice. Do the other side.

Despina.a7ed84ce.text: And nobody even lost a memory. Probably.

Despina.ae1b9bc7.text: Forgetting is a door, not a wall. You simply never look back through it.

Despina.bba84fa9.text: Forgetting is a door that opens only one way, little flame. Mind which side of it you stand on.

Despina.da6dc41d.text: Rude of them to stand there.

Despina.e1b9b641.text: No, no, no. Not you. Not today.

Despina.f303966b.text: Go on, little flames. The Court is watching. We so rarely get a show.

Despina.f8433cf9.text: I am Ysolde. I speak for the Glimmer Court. Come to the willow, little flames, and let us see what you have brought to trade.

Enceladus.0509ac01.text: Then it was for nothing. All of it, for nothing.

Enceladus.22a6e522.text: There. Clean. You'll want that bound.

Enceladus.31f6ba1f.text: Hm. You're quicker than you look.

Enceladus.59b77082.text: I'm fine. Physicians are the worst patients.

Enceladus.789a463a.text: Please don't make me do this. I've so little time left for anything else.

Enceladus.87f4d0a4.text: Go down the mountain. Get warm. Forget you came here.

Enceladus.8e427416.text: Hold still. It's worse if you move.

Enceladus.92ff92f0.text: Just under the ribs. I always did know where to cut.

Enceladus.93bac4b3.text: Time of death. No. I don't keep count any more.

Enceladus.9761cf82.text: I'm sorry. You're standing between me and the only thing I have left.

Enceladus.bd258562.text: Wait. Please. My notes. Don't burn my notes.

Enceladus.db2579af.text: They don't feel it. I checked. I checked so carefully.

Enceladus.e8cddb2a.text: Breathe slowly. This will be over soon.

Erinome.14bcfc9a.text: Retreat is a perfectly valid strategy!

Erinome.274e56ad.text: Exactly as the old treatises describe. With rather more shouting.

Erinome.441a3787.text: I've been counting the stars. There are fewer than in the old charts.

Erinome.62316667.text: Has anyone noticed the gaps in their memories? I'm keeping notes. In ink.

Erinome.6d44882b.text: Has anyone noticed how quiet the old songs go about the Hearthflame? I'm keeping notes.

Erinome.7bd51f67.text: This is less theoretical than I'd like.

Erinome.824c6847.text: Textbook. Literally; I've read the textbook.

Erinome.b2c50804.text: Mind the flanks. Statistically, that's where it goes wrong.

Erinome.ed3b27f4.text: I'll want to examine that later.

Fenrir.0726f773.text: Who's got the stew? I could eat a whole boar, tusks and all.

Fenrir.6394acee.text: Who's got the stew? I could eat a goblin. Not literally.

Fenrir.81c57220.text: Who's buying at the Last Coal?

Fenrir.b7962ce4.text: Just a scratch. A big one.

Gacrux.23c78b29.text: Don't touch the shards. Nothing that glows like that comes free.

Gacrux.728c6215.text: I can't sleep near the fire anymore. Don't ask me why. I don't know why.

Gacrux.c631a814.text: Don't touch the shards. Not if you want to keep your memories.

Gacrux.ce850ce1.text: I forget my mother's face. Did you know that? The fire took it.

Iapetus.03902685.text: Ha! Feel that? That's three winters of hunger!

Iapetus.03911840.text: Go home and tell them! The bridge is Vorga's!

Iapetus.1eacfa68.text: Ha. Ha. Fine. You win the bridge. You don't win the winter.

Iapetus.242ece5f.text: Get up! Nobody lies down on my bridge!

Iapetus.2f4d8457.text: Run back to your mayor. Tell him to open his granaries, or we come for them.

Iapetus.397060be.text: Not like this. Not to them.

Iapetus.3fb795e3.text: That's for the little ones! Every single one!

Iapetus.4d1b81e7.text: Down you go! Down where we've been all along!

Iapetus.4ed060ed.text: Again! Do it again, I dare you to stand up!

Iapetus.5c643fce.text: You think blood scares me? I was born hungry!

Iapetus.5de06e90.text: Host! Up, up! The valley's come visiting!

Iapetus.8b1feef5.text: Lucky! Stay lucky, valley folk. It won't last!

Iapetus.986ece2f.text: Look at them! Fat valley folk, all this way just to bleed!

Iapetus.c998e359.text: See? Taking works. Asking never fed anybody.

Iapetus.ec52b01f.text: You want my bridge? Come and take it! Come on, I'll wait!

Iapetus.f163a172.text: Every child who starved in the hills is watching you. Make it a good show!

Iapetus.fcb8bf7b.text: Ha! Ha ha! Is that all? My grandmother hits harder!

Kore.422f0e3e.text: Hold the line. I've got them.

Kore.d2b5e30f.text: Get some sleep. I'll take first watch.

Kore.e1db609c.text: Hold together. We do this properly.

Laomedeia.0129605a.text: Then listen close. This song is about your side of the mountain, a little. Perhaps it is about you.

Laomedeia.029e8167.text: You ask well. So, a crumb. In the old song the gold is not gold. We sing gold because it rhymes, and the true word is sad.

Laomedeia.0bd3bde1.text: Sit. You are guests now, which is worse than enemies. Guests we have to feed.

Laomedeia.0c4bb74a.text: Hm. Well fought. My grandson always said the valley would never share. I should have listened to him.

Laomedeia.10c39c3b.text: His friends will not like a truce. If they bare their teeth on the bridge, do not kill more of them than you must.

Laomedeia.10f68727.text: Seven came down when the snow was still falling, seven came down with their hands full of gold.

Laomedeia.1537e781.text: Here is the bargain, and it is a short one. Your town eats. My clan eats. The bridge goes back to being a bridge.

Laomedeia.1646935a.text: Whatever you think of me, feed the little ones. Feed them.

Laomedeia.28789e3a.text: Forty winters I have bled for this clan. Your turn.

Laomedeia.2a51ac9c.text: When the bellies are full, the clan sings. Tonight I sing the old one, because my bones say I should.

Laomedeia.2d77bb31.text: You fed my children. That makes you something. Not family. Not yet. Come back when you are.

Laomedeia.2df5e7c6.text: They will go to him. He will tell them they were brave. They were. Brave is cheap this winter.

Laomedeia.34d15c4e.text: Go down to the river. Tell it Skarrow sent you.

Laomedeia.36254136.text: Half? My children do not eat half. All of it, every week, or go home and fetch your captain.

Laomedeia.370e0656.text: But nobody runs when they carry a fortune. Seven came down, and the seven came running.

Laomedeia.47bc4643.text: Not yet. The little ones have not eaten.

Laomedeia.48c35900.text: My grandson's friends. They would rather die on the stones than eat valley bread. Foolish children.

Laomedeia.4b78081b.text: Come, then. My grandchildren are watching, and they are hungry.

Laomedeia.4fb20358.text: Ha! Somebody's mother taught you properly. You say my name like you have been scolded with it.

Laomedeia.539be9fc.text: You lock your grain and call us thieves. Now you come to finish it.

Laomedeia.5b42a283.text: Forty winters I have held this clan. Do not ask me if I can hold it one more.

Laomedeia.63290733.text: Half now, half at the thaw. You bargain like a hill grandmother. I will take it, and I will watch you.

Laomedeia.6eeeb0bf.text: Hm. I thought you smelled wrong. Not bad. Only far. Like snow from the other side.

Laomedeia.76466178.text: We took the bridge after. Not before. Tell your captain that, if she will hear it.

Laomedeia.7701c3e3.text: That is the next verse. And the next verse is not for strangers.

Laomedeia.793b1ff0.text: But you climbed the hill. So. Sit down again, and agree with me.

Laomedeia.823f544c.text: Your captain thinks. Good. Tell her to think about the grain.

Laomedeia.868c4aab.text: I see you, valley people. You came with spears after all. I hoped. I am old enough to know better than hope.

Laomedeia.875961c4.text: Hah. The hill is crooked. Like your mayor.

Laomedeia.879e8008.text: Not coin. Coin does not boil. A share of the grain your mayor keeps behind his locks. Every week, until the thaw.

Laomedeia.89ea0bf0.text: Up, little one. Up. Ah. No.

Laomedeia.917012d5.text: Your song was made by the ones who came home. Ours was made by the ones who watched them come.

Laomedeia.92e6c7da.text: Come, then. Every one of us you kill is one less mouth this winter. Your mayor will be so pleased.

Laomedeia.9688cc6d.text: So. The valley sends swords instead of grain. I expected it.

Laomedeia.a238995d.text: Valley people. Walking. Not running at me with spears. This is new.

Laomedeia.a5f0fd1c.text: Small kindness. Small stomachs. It is not nothing.

Laomedeia.a674fdbb.text: The valley song. Seven went over, seven came home, they brought something heavy. Yes. Pretty.

Laomedeia.a81e4dad.text: Seven went up where the wall meets the sky. No. Not for you. Not for the ones with spears.

Laomedeia.af275c1e.text: Do what you must. But I have buried enough of them this year. Leave me some to scold.

Laomedeia.b6928c58.text: Seven went up where the wall meets the sky, seven with nothing, and hungry, and cold.

Laomedeia.b76444af.text: Then you saw. My little ones were down on the bank, digging roots. Your people shot at them.

Laomedeia.bd7916d9.text: The rest when you are family. Not before. Now eat. You are too thin for valley people.

Laomedeia.bec70ec0.text: I have buried better than you. I will not be buried by you.

Laomedeia.c1c0ba68.text: Most of them. Some of the young ones belong to my grandson now, in their hearts. Vorga. He left us to take instead of ask.

Laomedeia.d274de5b.text: Go home. Tell them the bridge stays ours until the grain comes.

Laomedeia.d861d152.text: Two-day bread. From the innkeeper, yes? The one who feeds anybody.

Laomedeia.db10f60c.text: Then you know a hill word the valley does not have. It means a debt that both sides pretend is a gift.

Laomedeia.dcccc6e4.text: You lock your grain and call us thieves. Sit. We will talk about who stole what.

Laomedeia.ddf21f82.text: There was a song I meant to teach somebody. Too late now. It goes into the river with me.

Laomedeia.f850cfeb.text: Then it is agreed. Tell your mayor the old mother will give back his bridge. Tell him she is counting the sacks.

Leda.1e0f981f.text: You came! I told Bree you'd come. The mayor's been asking for you all day, and he's ever so cross.

Leda.255a68e2.text: It's so cold now. It was warm here, once. I remember it being warm.

Leda.2622a84e.text: The stars are wrong tonight. No. They're right. I just remember them different.

Leda.489a529a.text: I can run that for you! Two coppers. One if you're nice. Three if you're not.

Leda.4dafb332.text: I didn't take it. I was holding it. For you. Here.

Leda.74591c3b.text: There's a song in my head again. I never learned it. Want to hear?

Leda.7838ac77.text: That one came the same week as the goblins. Never eats. Never sleeps that I've seen. Bree says it's rude to stare.

Leda.8fa7ec9c.text: I dreamed the river was boiling again. Again's the wrong word, isn't it? I wasn't there.

Leda.9b9a9bb5.text: Can I sit with you? Just till I'm sleepy. I'm not scared. I'm cold.

Leda.afc3a87a.text: Tell me a story. A true one. I'll know if it isn't.

Leda.c51b0400.text: Down here. Under the third pier, past the eel traps. I don't know how I know that. I've never been under here.

Leda.da1f2739.text: Bree says I'm not to bother you. I'm not bothering. I'm standing.

Leda.df10fd65.text: I dreamed of a big stone hall with a fire in the middle. I've never been in a hall.

Leda.f0e96f71.text: I know a quicker way round the docks. Don't ask how. I just do.

Orus.100f98aa.text: Hm. That edge has seen work. Leave it with me.

Orus.3d6bcd97.text: Forge is cold this morning. Colder than yesterday.

Orus.40691a56.text: Shut the door. You're letting the heat out. What's left of it.

Orus.5f9a0165.text: Don't ask where the last shard came from. I didn't.

Orus.c4266628.text: Mm. Good steel remembers the hammer. Better than I do, some days.

Orus.c52a0b96.text: Four Fells at this anvil before me. I'll not be the one lets it go out.

Orus.e61475c4.text: Mm. Bring me the steel. I'll see what's left in the fire.

Pulcherrima.1c30b36e.text: Who's got the stew? I could eat a goblin. Not literally.

Pulcherrima.26bfc3bf.text: Who's buying at the Last Coal?

Pulcherrima.6a11f293.text: Just a scratch. A big one.

Pulcherrima.7182c432.text: Who's got the stew? I could eat a whole boar, tusks and all.

Rasalgethi.02c7aac0.text: So. It ends with tired hands, like everything else.

Rasalgethi.33a6af41.text: Go home. Remember this. Remember all of it.

Rasalgethi.35b68fc8.text: Every wound has a history. I will remember yours.

Rasalgethi.596fcb5d.text: I have been dying for a century. You will have to do better.

Rasalgethi.69918474.text: Sit down. Ah. No one ever sits.

Rasalgethi.73baf726.text: I will remember your name. Someone ought to.

Rasalgethi.a0322e5e.text: Hm. Clumsy. I was better at this, once.

Rasalgethi.ba8c16ea.text: You have come a very long way to be wrong.

Rasalgethi.c3914ccd.text: Pain. How very vivid. I had forgotten nothing but that.

Rasalgethi.df29d698.text: Not yet. There is still a thing I meant to finish.

Rasalgethi.fd9a2eb6.text: I have kept this hall for a hundred years. I will keep it a little longer.

Sadachbia.38f15175.text: Old Maud says I ask the wrong questions. She's usually right, which is infuriating.

Sadachbia.4f27bcd3.text: If you find anything written down out there, anything at all, bring it to me. Please.

Sadachbia.5a127754.text: Ink. Ink doesn't forget. That's the whole... yes. That's the whole point of ink.

Sadachbia.690be48d.text: Don't touch that pile, it's in order. It doesn't look in order. It is.

Sadachbia.b303661d.text: Mother Aubrine calls history a matter of faith. I call it a matter of paper.

Sadachbia.c24316e4.text: Thirty years in these records, and forty-one years are simply missing from them. Nobody else seems to mind.

Sadachbia.c888f978.text: Thirty years reading by ember-lamp, and I can't remember half of what I read. Odd, isn't it?

Sadachbia.d9170494.text: Forty-one years, simply missing. Who loses forty-one years? Unless...

Sadachbia.e01ff429.text: Ah, you're back! Good. I've found another gap. Well, not found. More... not found.

Sadaltager.08c4ba35.text: Exactly as the old treatises describe. With rather more shouting.

Sadaltager.09436a1d.text: I've been counting the stars. There are fewer than in the old charts.

Sadaltager.0bd85432.text: This is less theoretical than I'd like.

Sadaltager.1625a996.text: Because you came to a bridge and chose. Most people let the choosing happen to them. It matters more than you'd think.

Sadaltager.165ca873.text: Mind the flanks. Statistically, that's where it goes wrong.

Sadaltager.1bf837c2.text: I know the road you came by. It's longer than you remember. Don't ask me to walk it with you. Not yet.

Sadaltager.1f309cf2.text: She isn't the only one. There are four more. You'll want to reach them before the woman in grey does.

Sadaltager.201cf514.text: Don't thank me. You may not want to, later.

Sadaltager.2255da8e.text: Go and look at your bridge. It's older than your town, and it has seen this before.

Sadaltager.28a727ab.text: Whatever they ask for, think before you say yes. Things given in Mirewood stay given.

Sadaltager.32092c5e.text: Some fires are kept. Some are only borrowed. Few people know the difference.

Sadaltager.4262204f.text: Textbook. Literally; I've read the textbook.

Sadaltager.48afc5f1.text: Retreat is a perfectly valid strategy!

Sadaltager.4aceabcd.text: Sleep. The road keeps until morning. Most things do.

Sadaltager.59c593e8.text: Someone who has watched a great many rivers. You're asking the right questions. You're just asking the wrong people.

Sadaltager.60f3d594.text: The mountains look close tonight. They never are.

Sadaltager.633a2ce5.text: The nearest lies in Mirewood, where the marsh began to dream. The Court there will want something for it.

Sadaltager.684c4aad.text: Has anyone noticed how quiet the old songs go about the Hearthflame? I'm keeping notes.

Sadaltager.6c002256.text: I'll want to examine that later.

Sadaltager.7867142d.text: Has anyone noticed the gaps in their memories? I'm keeping notes. In ink.

Sadaltager.833d7706.text: We've met before. No? Then we will.

Sadaltager.8be0b877.text: Lovely evening. It won't last. They never do.

Sadaltager.932886ec.text: You found her. Good. She hasn't long, you know. Cracked and chipped, and cold at the heart. Like most things in this valley.

Sadaltager.9d63f457.text: The child sings well. Has anyone asked her where she learned?

Sadaltager.d7f741c4.text: She'll keep better near her sisters than in the mud. Leave her here, and the Ash Market will have her in chips by spring.

Sadaltager.ebcb11cb.text: You remember well, Maud. Better than anyone. That was always going to be a problem for somebody.

Schedar.17898565.text: The gate is yours. I held it as long as I was able.

Schedar.2e1f36a5.text: Come, then. It has been a long while since anyone tried.

Schedar.42501191.text: Ah. There it is. I had nearly forgotten what this felt like.

Schedar.5f3be127.text: Steady. The oath holds, even when I do not.

Schedar.6644cb1b.text: A fair stroke, I hope. I try to keep them clean.

Schedar.73a218ee.text: My apologies. That one will not heal kindly.

Schedar.a00c306a.text: I hold this gate for the Keeper. You have my apologies, and my blade.

Schedar.a4fcfe51.text: Well fought. I thank you. I thank you most sincerely.

Schedar.d1af1b76.text: Go back down the mountain. Live long. Do not come again.

Schedar.e9076bc4.text: Well met. I regret, sincerely, what comes next.

Sulafat.09c96d59.text: I don't want to hurt you. I want you warm. Both can be true today.

Sulafat.451c0d11.text: Grain for peace. That's beautiful, truly. And when the grain runs out, and the ground goes cold? Kindness won't warm it.

Sulafat.45e0c7b6.text: Rest now. When you wake, it will be warm.

Sulafat.52b79d99.text: I'll remember you kindly. I remember everyone kindly.

Sulafat.54462050.text: One hurt now, ten thousand spared. I've done the sums.

Sulafat.71b02bf9.text: Kindled, rise. The cold doesn't care if you're tired.

Sulafat.7399eb5e.text: Still standing. Good. There's still time to listen.

Sulafat.85b97cd4.text: I had a plan. I was the only one with a plan.

Sulafat.9422c710.text: Then who keeps them warm? Tell me that. Who?

Sulafat.965686b3.text: You've felt the cold. Stand with me, or stand aside.

Sulafat.97f3d2fa.text: It doesn't have to be this way. The Hearthflame can burn again. It wants to. It only needs us to be brave enough to feed it.

Sulafat.9fbc0f8b.text: I'm sorry. I'll carry that one too.

Sulafat.a407c9aa.text: You found it, didn't you? Under the docks. I can see it on you. Tell me, what did the ford cost you?

Sulafat.a81e33f9.text: Your warmth goes into the flame now. It won't be wasted.

Sulafat.c472266b.text: Not yet. They're all counting on me.

Sulafat.cc36f386.text: You've felt how cold it's getting. The fields. The forges. Your own hearths, a little lower every year.

Sulafat.ce27c406.text: Mother Aubrine. You fed half this town last winter, and you'll bury the other half this one. I'm offering more than prayers.

Sulafat.edc72231.text: Every winter we argue, more children freeze. Let's not argue.

Sulafat.f1bea43d.text: Come and find me when you're ready to save the Vale, and not only this town. I'll be wherever the embers are.

Sulafat.f714da20.text: Then you understand already. Sometimes one life buys a winter for a thousand. That isn't cruelty. It's arithmetic.

Sulafat.fcf5927e.text: I've felt worse. I remember being worse.

Umbriel.0f6a78f0.text: Here's something for free, since I'm feeling generous. I sell more shards than this ember has to give.

Umbriel.1e0fe471.text: Mind the docks after dark. Not everyone down here is as friendly as me.

Umbriel.44e9d184.text: Fine. Put it on my tab.

Umbriel.457031ab.text: She was dying long before I came. I sell the pieces before they're worth nothing. That's not murder. That's timing.

Umbriel.4df7e8a4.text: There you are. Wondered when the river would bring you back. You still owe me, you know.

Umbriel.6c66359e.text: You didn't see me. That one's free.

Umbriel.7705fd5a.text: Everybody wants the same thing in the end. I just get there first.

Umbriel.805db8d9.text: Last offer. Walk away and I forget your faces.

Umbriel.81685659.text: Shards, word, a boat at midnight. All for sale. Which do you need?

Umbriel.a572e698.text: Rook. I run the Ash Market. You've bought from me, or your grandmother did. Everyone has.

Umbriel.b53f5a4f.text: Funny thing. I'm selling more shards than the Vale ought to have. Don't spread that about.

Umbriel.c2f15317.text: Yes, we chip her. A shard here, a shard there, and somebody's hearth stays warm. Shame to let it go to waste in the mud.

Umbriel.c81bb511.text: Somebody else supplies the difference. I don't know who. I'd like to, before they decide they don't need me.

Umbriel.caf09b79.text: All right. All right. Let's talk terms.

Umbriel.caf2184d.text: Prices went up. Everything's colder, and cold costs.

Umbriel.cb99b723.text: Here's how you pay. I'm selling the Kindled more shards than exist in the Vale. Find who's supplying the rest, and we're square.

Umbriel.e29071c8.text: Careful. You're standing on my livelihood.

Vindemiatrix.0643e496.text: I buried two this week, old ones, cold in their beds. Pray it stays only the old.

Vindemiatrix.152fd558.text: Come in out of the wind. There's soup at the back, and nobody counts the bowls.

Vindemiatrix.3e5cda96.text: We were all warming our hands at a fire you knew was dying. Gods forgive you, Halden. I'm not sure I can, yet.

Vindemiatrix.4410ca9d.text: Maren Sorrel. I put you out of my chapel once. Don't make me do it to the whole square.

Vindemiatrix.4cc57b2f.text: Mind how you speak in the square. Fear spreads faster than fever.

Vindemiatrix.68c86225.text: But you came home when I wrote to you. Here. The archive key. Bring it back, and bring me what you find.

Vindemiatrix.831a18f3.text: You always did find the sharp end of a sermon. Very well. The chapel opens its stores first, and in public.

Vindemiatrix.8da99f5f.text: The chapel can spare its tithe barley. It isn't much. But no one sent to my door has ever been turned away.

Vindemiatrix.8e16f7e4.text: Pray if you like. If you'd rather not, sit anyway. The chapel doesn't mind.

Vindemiatrix.a29eef99.text: Doubt is a draught under the door. Shut it, and keep the hearth.

Vindemiatrix.a649f7ee.text: Corvin says the records have holes in them. Corvin says a great many things.

Vindemiatrix.c2513b6a.text: Then we shall see who in this room is willing to be seen giving less than the church.

Vindemiatrix.cbdc6077.text: Be careful of her. The worst of it is that she believes every word.

Vindemiatrix.ecdca431.text: The flame was given to us. We will be worthy of it, cold or warm.

Vindemiatrix.f634b447.text: The cellar texts? No one has read those in my lifetime. They're very old, and very dull, I'm told.

Zephyr.02311538.text: I'll keep the stew warm. For whoever comes back across.

Zephyr.04bf9fbe.text: She sent a little one down for bread in the spring. Asked at the granary gate, polite as you like.

Zephyr.11f3a189.text: Stew's hot, bread's yesterday's. Don't complain, my love, nobody else is feeding you.

Zephyr.163bb66a.text: My best rooms. He means my only rooms. Still. Done.

Zephyr.2b0fe173.text: Heard a thing at the bar you'll want to hear. Eat first.

Zephyr.2eb01dac.text: And the ones who don't break, Dagna? The ones with nowhere left to run to?

Zephyr.50ffb190.text: Pip! Where's that girl got to? Never mind. She'll turn up when she's hungry.

Zephyr.57211e76.text: Oh, no you don't. Up you get, my love. Up!

Zephyr.6390da08.text: Come in closer. The fire doesn't bite, and neither do I. Much.

Zephyr.6c380dd7.text: Boots off the benches. I'll not tell you twice. Well, I will, but I'll not like it.

Zephyr.76af17da.text: I'm all right. I'm all right. Keep going.

Zephyr.8fe64c92.text: Bread. Two days old, but it's honest. Take it up the hill. Children first, mind.

Zephyr.99639f3f.text: And here's mine. That's a whole people up there, and they're hungry for the same reason we are, only worse.

Zephyr.9d5e4532.text: Pip, let them breathe. You lot, there's stew when he's done with you. Don't let him talk it cold.

Zephyr.a60b216f.text: Leaner for them. We had the warm fields. They had snow on their fires by the Harvest Month.

Zephyr.aeacefe3.text: Brought you a pie. Don't look at me like that, you're thin as rakes, the lot of you.

Zephyr.c3f9e45f.text: Right then. I've thrown worse than you out of my inn.

Zephyr.cd4b734f.text: Sit. Eat. Then you can tell me how bad it is.

Zephyr.cf40c03a.text: Good. Now everyone's coming back for supper, and no arguments.

Zephyr.ef329ccf.text: Bad dreams and too much cheese, that's all. In you come, Pip. Bed.

Zephyr.f2a2cb51.text: Thank you, my love. Your supper is on the house.

Zephyr.f49fbc2d.text: Kill their mother and you've bought a bridge for one winter. Her grandsons will remember it for fifty.

Zubenelgenubi.0eba04cc.text: I'm fine. Mostly fine. Ask me again in a minute.

Zubenelgenubi.1e88eaac.text: Oh, that's nice. Do the other side.

Zubenelgenubi.435389f8.text: And nobody even lost a boot. A small miracle.

Zubenelgenubi.713bcca3.text: That went better than my last plan.

Zubenelgenubi.8b915fee.text: No, no, no. Not you. Not today.

Zubenelgenubi.a195f95b.text: One day I'll sleep in a real bed. With a pillow. Two pillows.

Zubenelgenubi.b8d4ea15.text: Does anyone else remember what we had for breakfast? No? Just me, then. Hopefully.

Zubenelgenubi.d91f4576.text: And nobody even lost a memory. Probably.

Zubenelgenubi.f32e6ba4.text: Rude of them to stand there.
